What changed in the plant, and why

The 2026-09-19 tranche (page) ended with every hand holding 64 of 64 in the benchmark and most of them dropping the tool inside the UR5e chain. Re-evaluating the same checkpoints with the tool spawned 3 mm and 10° off the trained pose gave the reason: training had spawned the tool at one pose (cube_spawn_xy_jitter 0), the evaluator inherited it, and the 64 rollouts were one rollout under 64 GPU contact solves. Under the jitter D7 held 0 of 64, the D6 clip seed 1 8, D5 26, D1 20; the D6 separation policy 64. Three more differences between the training plant and the plant every CPU replay, chain rollout and bench comparison runs on came out while chasing that number:

After the turn: re-pose, set-down, relay handover, gait

The probe does not stop when the policy’s 5 s end: the fingers freeze at their last set-point and the chain continues with its own stages, the arm re-posing the palm so the shaft points down, lowering the shaft into the post’s hole, the relay handover (one finger re-grips at a time, the tool never released) and eight gait cycles. Each cell is the tool’s cos to vertical and its height at that seam; gaited is the last. The gait’s screw turns are the rotation the cycles put into the shaft; a chain that stands the tool and gaits 8 cycles at 0.00 turns is holding it without driving it.

The gait does not move the fingers on this plant. Finger commands and joint angles recorded every 60 sim steps through the D6 clip run at plate 0 (r_d6_clip_chain_pl0_ctrl_qpos.json): through the eight cycles the commanded angles vary by 5–27° per joint (the ring table is built around the tool’s actual axis, 31 mm of IK residual) and the achieved angles by 0.3–9°; the index pip sits 59° behind its command for the whole gait (commanded 88°, achieved 26–31°), the thumb and middle 3–15°. The tool stands in the hole under 20 N of pad force and turns −0.002 revolutions. This is the 2026-09-16 result on the calibrated chain (fingers 14–38° behind command through the gait, 0.00–0.02 rev) with the policy’s turn in front of it; the chain’s ok gate tests stance, grip and cycles run, not screw turns. The relay handover does move the fingers (commands change by 77–110° on the index, achieved 21–44°) and the tool stays at cos 0.99 through it.

Plate height: the chain scenes in assets/mjcf/experimental/20260904-chain_bothsets/ were generated with the palm plate at the mounting plane; the built hand carries it at +25 mm, which is where the training scenes put it. The probe moves the plate per run (plate_variant, a __plate25.xml beside the scene; only the plate geom moves), so the plate-25 rows are the built hand and the plate-0 rows the old geometry. The one film below is the plate-0 run; the plate-25 films are below it.

What decides the set-down is the angle the tool has when the arm has finished levelling it over the socket (staged). The tip sits 50 mm from the tool’s centre, so the tip’s lateral offset from the aimed centre is 50 mm × sin(angle) against a 6 mm capture radius: 8° is 7 mm and enters, 14° is 12 mm and lands on the annulus beside the hole. D6 clip at plate 0 staged at cos 0.99 (8°) and entered; at plate 25 the same policy staged at 0.97 (14°), the separation policy at 0.95 (18°) and D5 at 0.89 (27°), and in each film the tip comes down beside the hole. D6 clip then loses the tool at the handover grip (it tips off the post); D5 and the separation policy keep it in hand leaning on the post at 47–55° through the gait. The staging already iterates the palm against the measured tool pose (eight corrections), so the residual angle is what the compliant grip gives back under the arm’s re-pose.

Aiming the tip at the seat instead of levelling the tool first

The residual angle does not have to close before the descent. The chain commands the tool’s pose and derives the palm’s from it (_rigid_palm_pose), and it already measures the tool’s low point every correction, so the staging and the descent can carry the apex over the socket rather than the body centre, and the lean can come out afterwards as a rotation about the seated tip with the floor carrying the weight (the _upright(about_foot) move the pivot order already uses). real_v1_chain_policy.py --seat-aim tip does that: _stage aims the measured apex at place_xy, _descend takes one aim on the apex at the top of its move, and a seated phase follows the set-down (eight corrections about the apex, walking it onto the socket centre). The shipped behaviour is --seat-aim centre, which is what every other chain row on this page ran.

On the three plate-25 policies that hold the turn, the set-down now lands the apex within 1.5 mm of the socket centre at the lean the grip gives it (15.5°, 30.5° and 12.9°), the seated correction takes the lean to 7.0°, 1.5° and 2.8°, and all three keep the tool through the relay handover and the eight gait cycles: D5 at 0.4°, D6 clip at 6.3° with 17.4 N on the pads, D6 with separation at 2.9° with 16.7 N. The chain’s ok passes at the built plate height for the first time. The turns column is unchanged at 0.00: the gait’s achieved-angle problem is the next item and this change does not touch it. Rows are tilt / tool centre z (mm; the seated centre is at 49.5) / pads on the tool at each seam.

The handover and the gait on the calibrated plant: the loop, the command reference and the ring’s reach

The 2026-09-16 measurement, run on the three seated policies. An achieved-joint-angle loop (--angle-gain k: command = set-point + k × (set-point − achieved), slewed 0.01 rad per tick, clipped at 0.45 rad, armed from the press so the RL turn runs as trained) does not close the error, and the seams say why. At the press the servos are already on their ceiling: the thumb sits 76° short of its set-point on D6 with an actuator at 0.35 N·m, the index 28°. The set-point is the policy’s last action, a residual frozen at its ±1 rad clip, 70–79° past the achieved angle on every hand at turned; the chain’s 0.3 mm regrip, the relay’s pinned pads and the gait table’s rebase are all measured from that command, so every later grip inherits the saturation. The loop’s trim hits its 26° band at once, sat rises to 2–3 actuators per finger, and the gait gains 3° in its first cycles and stops (+0.02 turns). The command-referenced design is right on the kp-30 plant, where the deflection it preserves is a millimetre; here it is a radian.

Re-seeding the command from the achieved angles (_squeeze_cmd(from_achieved=True)) takes the servos off the ceiling. Done right after the turn with the plans’ 10 mm (--regrip-ref achieved --carry-squeeze 10) the grip drops from 16 N to 5 N; on D6 clip the arm then stages at 3.2° instead of 13°, seats at 0.3°, and with the angle loop on top the gait turns the screw 6.0, 3.1, 2.4, 1.9, 1.9, 2.3, 4.3, 3.9° per cycle, +0.071 turns in 8 cycles at a final tilt of 0.8°, the first non-zero turn on the calibrated plant. On D5 and the separation policy the same 3–4 N grip does not survive the arm’s levelling from 32–35° of lean (lost before staged). Done at the press instead (--press-regrip 10), where the seat carries the tool, all three keep it (D6 clip 76/28/3° → 11/12/13°, sat 0) and the handover then drives the index 45–102° short and onto the ceiling on every run: the relay’s ring target is 17–27 mm beyond the finger’s reach (ring_ik_grip_mm, the same 20 mm the 2026-09-06 D6 chain carried, where a rigid finger turned an unreachable command into force). The gait then turns 5–6° in its first cycle and stalls. The slide handover, written for a reachable ring with the grasp unbroken, moves the palm 49 mm and 45° to the gait’s pose and pulls the tool out of the seat (z 53 → 82–96 mm). Training curves

Training pipeline: architecture and the decisions behind it

A policy on this page is a 9-dimensional residual on a scripted grasp-and-lift, trained by PPO on 3072 copies of one hand’s frozen scene in MuJoCo-Warp through mjlab, and warm-started from one D6 run of 2026-09-17. This section is the whole of that pipeline as it stands on 2026-09-20: the stages from the hardware model to a checkpoint, one episode, what the actor reads and writes, the reward and the terminations, the optimiser, the warm-start lineage, and a register of every setting with the reason on record and whether that reason is a measurement. The tables are read from the run configuration of the first finished job, so their numbers are the tranche’s own.

Stages, from the hardware model to a checkpoint

  1. Hand. assets/mjcf/real_v1/real_hand.xml is the CAD-matched three-finger hand; real_v1_design_search.py draws mount coordinates and link lengths from a Sobol sequence inside REAL_V1_WORKSPACE, filters on servo range, gantry travel and finger clearance, and the eight promoted hands (D1–D8) were built and run on the bench. The morphology is frozen into the scene (freeze_scene_for_eval) so no morphology joint drifts during a rollout.
  2. Grasp. The chain fitter places the three pads on the shaft at or below its equator and writes the open_ik keyframe (finger joints with the pads just off the shaft) and the grip anchor (the same pose closed by a 10 mm commanded squeeze). There is no CEM on these scenes; the anchor is the deployed plan’s own grip.
  3. Plant. apply_measured_plant.py rewrites the scene to the servo sysid of 2026-09-02 (finger kp 0.5, kv 0.02, forcerange 0.35 N·m, frictionloss 0.0035, measured link masses), the elliptic friction cone with impratio 10, and the +25 mm palm plate the bench carries. The result is the _cal morphology run (results/phase1/real_v1/20260916-<hand>_cal), which also holds the open-loop reference rollout of that grip and lift (best_rollout.npz) that the tracking terms and the ref_* observations use.
  4. Tool. make_tipmesh_morphology_run.py derives the _cal_tip run: the 25 mm screwdriver shaft with the screw-tip mesh the chain and the bench carry (25.6 g). This tranche is the first to train on it.
  5. Environment. morphohand.rl.env_build turns the frozen scene into an mjlab task: the hand as the robot entity, the tool as an object entity that keeps the scene’s contact class and mesh assets, the scene’s own floor (--scene-floor), 2 ms physics, control at 50 Hz. Observations, rewards, terminations and reset events are the managers listed below; the finger action term is the eased set-point plus the residual, the palm action term is the scripted lift.
  6. Optimiser. rl_train_cube.py --recipe b_liveA loads the blessed reorient recipe (the B10 reward block, the deploy-parity residual scale and easing, the contact gate, the relaxed slip guards) and the CLI adds the run-specific knobs; the trainer is rsl_rl PPO with the collapse watchdog attached. A warm start copies the parent’s actor and critic tensor by tensor.
  7. Evaluation. The checkpoint is scored on 64 nominal and 64 jittered GPU rollouts, replayed on the CPU solver under the transfer variants, run through the UR5e chain at both plates, and filmed; the numbers on this page are those, never the reward.

One episode

What the actor reads and writes

term dims meaning actor noise (uniform)
joint_pos 15 9 finger + 6 palm joint positions relative to default ±0.01 rad
joint_vel 15 their velocities ±0.5 rad/s
object_pos 3 tool position relative to the palm site ±5 mm
object_pose_actual 7 tool position and quaternion in the palm frame ±5 mm
ref_finger_qpos 9 finger joints of the open-loop reference rollout at this step none
ref_object_pose 7 tool pose of the reference rollout at this step none
actions 9 the actor’s previous output none
target_axis_misalign 1 1 − cos between the shaft axis and vertical none

The actor is an MLP 512-256-128 (elu) from the 66 inputs to 9 Gaussian means with a learned per-dimension standard deviation (initial 0.3); the critic has the same shape and reads the same 66 terms without noise. Each action is clipped to ±2.0 by the rsl_rl wrapper and multiplied by 0.5 rad before it is added to the finger set-point, so the residual is bounded at ±1.0 rad and is zero before policy step 58. The palm has no learned degree of freedom: its six joints follow the scripted lift (enable_palm_rotation_residual false).

Reward

term weight shape active
target_axis_alignment 100 exp(−4(1 − cos)²), cos between the shaft axis and world +z from step 58
target_axis_progress 300 cos(t) − cos(t − 1), signed from step 58
contact_min 15 indicator: all 3 pads on the tool all episode
object_lateral_drift −8 |xy − xy_spawn| beyond a 10 mm deadband, power 2, contact-gated all episode
object_xy_drift −3 xy drift from the reference, contact-gated all episode
object_orientation_drift −3 orientation drift from the reference, contact-gated all episode
finger_drift_from_grip −2 finger joints away from the grip pose, contact-gated all episode
action_rate_l2 −0.005 |a(t) − a(t − 1)|² all episode
grip_force_excess −2 mean over pads of (max(F − 6 N, 0) / 4)² all episode
finger_separation_penalty 0 in the clip arm; −10 in the separation arm (max(d_min − clearance, 0) / d_min)² on the index–middle link chains, d_min 30 mm all episode
track_finger_qpos 4 exp(−20·|q − q_ref|²) against the open-loop rollout of the fitted grip all episode
track_object_pos 6 exp(−200·|p − p_ref|²) all episode
track_object_quat 2 exp(−10·quat error²) all episode
track_finger_ctrl_anchor 1 exp(−4·|ctrl − anchor|²), keeps the set-point near the grip all episode
contact_mean 10 mean pad-contact indicator all episode
lift_height 80 object height above spawn, clipped at the 100 mm target lift phase
object_drop −12 indicator: object 20 mm below spawn lift phase
fingertip_to_object −3 mean pad-to-shaft distance all episode
joint_pos_limits −2 joint excursion beyond its range all episode

mjlab multiplies every term by the control period (0.02 s), so a weight of 100 is 2 per step. The tracking terms follow the open-loop rollout of the fitted grip on the same scene (best_rollout.npz in the morphology run); the contact gate zeroes a stability term while the mean pad-contact indicator is below 0.5.

Terminations

termination condition effect
time_out 5 s (250 steps) the normal end
object_drop tool 20 mm below its spawn height during the lift phase (from step 58) ends the episode
tip_lost fewer than 3 pads on the tool for 15 consecutive steps, from step 58 ends the episode
object_slip / orientation_slip / finger_slip 0.5 m / 10 rad / 100 rad thresholds the recipe set out of reach: they never fire
collapse watchdog the trainer aborts when the episode-mean object height falls below 0.03 m after iteration 40 a run that has dropped the tool stops costing GPU time

Optimiser

PPO
environments × steps per iteration 3072 × 24 = 73,728 samples
iterations 271 for 20 M steps
epochs × minibatches 5 × 4
learning rate 0.0005, adaptive on a KL target of 0.01
γ, λ, clip, entropy 0.99, 0.95, 0.2, 0.005
value loss, gradient clip 1 (clipped), 1
checkpoints every 50 iterations; model_270.pt is the one evaluated
seed none is applied: rl_train_cube.py parses --seed and never uses it, mjlab’s environment seed stays None and the rsl_rl config field (42) is not read by the runner; every run, s0/s1/s2 included, is an unseeded draw

Warm-start lineage

  1. 2026-09-17, D6 from scratch, 60 M steps (20260917-1141-d6_cal_reorient_gp025_60M_s0): the b_liveA recipe on the D6 _cal scene, residual ±0.5 rad from step 58, friction DR, sighted. Held 64/64 at cos 0.933; the tool rolls across the pads from step 68 with the thumb load rising 3 → 12 N; total pad force 17–18 N. The grip term in that run had the wrong sign (+0.25, a bonus). The alignment reward was still rising at 60 M.
  2. 2026-09-17, grip finetune, 20 M (ft_gpm5): actor and critic warm-started, penalty −5 above 4 N; cos 0.969 at 10.8 N. In the chain on 2026-09-19 it turned to 0.91 and dropped at 3.2 s; the 17 N parent held 3/4. The tranche therefore warm-starts from the parent and penalises only above 6 N.
  3. 2026-09-19 tranche, 16 jobs, 20 M each: the 60 M parent continued on each hand’s _cal scene with the action clip at 2.0 (residual ±1 rad), the −2 / 6 N grip penalty, and for six jobs the separation term. All arms sighted (a blind warm start had not recovered in 22 iterations). Clip 2.0 held 64/64 on every hand at the trained pose and collapsed under ±3 mm of spawn jitter on D7, D6 s1, D5 and D1.
  4. 2026-09-20 tranche (this page), 12 jobs, 20 M each: each 2026-09-19 checkpoint continued on the _cal_tip scene with the scene floor, the scene’s contact class, spawn jitter ±3 mm / ±10° and friction DR.

Decision register

Every setting the tranche runs under, with the reason the record gives and whether that reason is a measurement. “Inherited” means the value was carried from an earlier phase of the program (the m05 / b33 lineage of June–July or the first real_v1 scripts of late August) and has not been re-measured on the calibrated real_v1 plant.

decision value since reason on record status
Hand provenance eight deployed real_v1 hands (D1–D8) from the 8,198-hand Sobol population; sv1_*, g12, rv05 2026-08-27/28 only hands generated from assets/mjcf/real_v1/real_hand.xml and exportable through the plan pipeline count; all eight were run on hardware (251 runs) measured
Grasp chain-fitter anchor, open_ik keyframe, pads at or below the shaft equator, 10 mm commanded squeeze 2026-08-27, 2026-09-16 pads above the equator wedge the shaft out in 0.6 s of standing still (SLIP.md); at kp 0.5 a 2 mm squeeze lifts at 0.16–1.43 N, 10 mm at 2.5–4.5 N on 3–4 pads, which is what the exported plans carry measured
Finger plant kp 0.5, kv 0.02, forcerange 0.35 N·m, frictionloss 0.0035, elliptic cone with impratio 10, pad μ 1.0, palm plate +25 mm 2026-09-02, 2026-09-16 the shipped kp 30 predicts a +0.03° deficit where the bench measures +11.7°; the corrected plant drops 6 % of jittered trials against the bench’s 8 % measured (servo sysid, drop gate)
Tool and floor screw-tip mesh (25.6 g), the scene’s floor and contact class inside mjlab 2026-09-20 the object entity had trained on MuJoCo’s default solref/solimp on mjlab’s plane since the first mjlab run; the chain and the bench carry the tip measured (this page)
Control 9 finger residuals on a set-point that eases (quadratic ease-out) from the open keyframe to the grip anchor over 80 sim steps; residual = 0.5 rad × action, action clipped to ±2 scale 0.5: 2026-07; clip 2.0: 2026-09-19 action 0 reproduces the open-loop grasp and lift (lesson 6); 0.5 rad was Policy B’s budget hardcoded into every screen and the bench manoeuvres wanted more; at clip 2.0 every hand held 64/64 where the ±0.5 rad parents had not turned clip measured; scale inherited from the July deploy-parity setting
Residual onset step 58 (sim step 580): 0.52 s after the 80-step lift ramp ends; the reorient reward and the tip-lost termination start there too 2026-08-30 the tool settles on the pads after the lift (4.9 mm of servo settling at 0.52 s measured in the chain on 2026-09-20) inherited; the settling measurement is consistent with it
Reorient reward alignment 100 × exp(−4(1 − cos)²) + progress 300 × Δcos per step, contact_min 15, lateral drift −8 2026-06 (B10 block, b33 lineage) the progress term gives a dense gradient toward vertical where the exponential alone is flat; the block is the one the m05 handoff converged under inherited; never re-swept on real_v1
Grip penalty −2 × mean over pads of (max(F − 6 N, 0) / 4)² 2026-09-19 20:30 the 10.8 N finetune (−5 above 4 N) turned to 0.91 in the chain and dropped at 3.2 s; the 17 N parent held 3/4, so the tranche keeps the parent’s grip and penalises only above 6 N measured in the chain; the value was not swept
Separation term −10 × (max(30 mm − clearance, 0) / 30 mm)² on the index–middle link chains (the “separation” arm) 2026-09-19 the bench index and middle carry servo housings and cabling the capsules omit; policies that run them together fail on hardware. It turns D1/D3/D5/D6 with more clearance and kills the turn on D4 (−3.6 mm) and D7 (1.1 mm) measured; the 30 mm threshold is not calipered
Terminations drop 20 mm below spawn; fewer than 3 pads for 15 consecutive steps; the slip guards at 0.5 m / 10 rad / 100 rad never fire recipe 2026-07; 15 steps since 2026-08-30 the recipe lets only drop and tip-lost end an episode (lesson 8: never strip them). The recipe’s 3 steps became 15 in train_real_v1_blind_pair.sh; no measurement behind the 15 is on record inherited
Domain randomisation friction ×[0.55, 1.15] on every geom per reset; observation noise ±0.01 rad, ±0.5 rad/s, ±5 mm; spawn ±3 mm / ±10° (this tranche) friction and noise 2026-07; spawn 2026-09-20 the 2026-09-19 policies collapse at ±3 mm (D7 0/64, D6 s1 8/64). Compliance DR is off since 2026-07-10: it relocated the policy to the band’s middle instead of broadening it spawn measured; friction band and noise inherited
Observation sighted 66-dim actor (object pose in the palm frame included); critic sees the same terms without noise 2026-08-30 (asymmetric), 2026-09-19 (sighted) a blind warm start had not recovered in 22 iterations and the bench tag tracker supplies the object pose at 50 Hz; blinding keeps the vector 66 wide (scale 0) so the warm start still loads measured once
Optimiser PPO (rsl_rl), 3072 envs × 24 steps per iteration, 5 epochs × 4 minibatches, lr 5·10⁻⁴ adaptive on KL 0.01, γ 0.99, λ 0.95, clip 0.2, entropy 0.005, initial std 0.3, MLP 512-256-128 ELU 2026-07 the GPU is compute-saturated at ~10 k steps/s and num_envs buys nothing; the rest are rsl_rl defaults inherited
Budget 20 M steps (271 iterations, ~36 min) per finetune; 60 M for the from-scratch D6 parent 2026-09-17/19 the 60 M parent was still gaining +8 % alignment per 160 iterations; the 20 M grip finetune moved cos 0.933 → 0.969 measured once; continued policies here end 30–45° short, so 20 M on the harder plant is the open item

Seeding none: --seed is parsed and never applied (its only mention is the argument itself), mjlab’s environment seed is None 2026-07 found while writing this register; the GPU contact solver is non-deterministic in any case, so two runs of one recipe have always been two draws (the two 60 M D6 runs differ by 0.29 in cos) defect; seed the trainer after the queue and keep evaluating as a distribution
Timing 5 s episodes, 2 ms physics, control at 50 Hz (decimation 10) 2026-07 the bench servo bus closes a loop at 50–111 Hz inherited

The numbers on this page

number how it is produced what it means

jittered the same with --spawn-jitter-mm 3 --spawn-yaw-deg 10 --friction-dr the judging number: 64 deterministic rollouts at one pose are one rollout under solver noise

chain real_v1_chain_policy.py --stages policy: UR5e lift on the menagerie arm at kp ×10, finger gravcomp off, the policy shadowed from step 0, plates 25 and 0 mm the first active observation matches the benchmark within 1° / 1.3 mm / 0.015 quat; what remains is the maneuver

Inherited settings and the measurement that would settle each

  • Tip-lost 15 steps. One hand (D6), two 20 M continuations from the same checkpoint at 3 and 15 consecutive steps, jittered hold and chain at both plates. The 3-step value ends a turn in which a pad lifts for 0.1 s; the 15-step value lets a two-pad pinch persist for 0.3 s.
  • The B10 reward block (100 / 300 / 15 / −8). A one-factor sweep of the progress weight (100, 300, 900) on D6 at the same budget, judged on jittered hold and end cos; the progress term is the one that pays for turning past 60°.
  • Friction DR band [0.55, 1.15]. μ 0.6 sits inside the band and still drops D1/D2 64/64 (2026-09-19); a band [0.4, 1.4] on one hand tells whether width helps or whether the policy relocates to the band’s middle as the compliance DR did.
  • Observation noise (±0.01 rad, ±0.5 rad/s, ±5 mm). The bench servo telemetry and the tag tracker have their own error (0.03 mm rms on the tag; joint positions in commanded units against a 0.018°/load-unit spring): the noise should be set from those, and a run with the tracker’s measured latency in the observation delay slot is the deploy-parity check.
  • Residual scale 0.5 rad and clip 2.0. The bound is stated in policy units; a scale-1.0 clip-1.0 run gives the same ±1 rad bound with a different exploration std and would show whether the bound or the std carried the 2026-09-19 gain.
  • 20 M steps on the harder plant. One 60 M continuation of r_d6_clipsep (the first item under Next steps).

Lessons from the two tranches

  • Evaluate off the trained pose. A deterministic evaluator on a zero-jitter environment measures the GPU solver, not the policy. policy_eval_suite.py --spawn-jitter-mm 3 --spawn-yaw-deg 10 --friction-dr is now the number a policy is judged on, and the driver writes it for every job (*_eval_j3dr.json).
  • The training plant was not the calibrated plant. Three defects between the frozen scene and the mjlab environment (tool contact class, floor, tip) had been there since the first mjlab run; the CPU replay, the chain and the bench comparison all ran on the scene. Any earlier sim-to-sim gap is confounded by them.
  • Reading the arm. The 4.9 mm the palm sat below its command at the seam was the menagerie servo settling (slow pole kp/kv = 5 rad/s), not load: with the payload declared a UR5e holds ~0.1 mm, and the chain now runs the arm at ten times the position gain.
  • Two silent no-ops. The friction variants of the zero-shot table were copies of the base scene on every calibrated scene until 2026-09-20 02:00 (the variant matched the template’s μ 2.4), and --payload-gravcomp had been compensating the finger links as well as the hand. Both fixed.
  • The separation term. −10 below 30 mm buys 2–10 mm of index–middle clearance on D1/D3/D5/D6 and takes the turn away from D4 and D7, which turn by running the two fingers together; on the matched plant the continued policies sit at 16–29 mm without it.
  • The chain’s ok is a hold, not a gait. The gate tests stance, grip and cycles run; on the calibrated plant the gait’s commands move the fingers 0.3–9° (index pip 59° behind its command) and put −0.002 turns into the screw. A chain that reads ok has stood the tool and held it for eleven seconds.
  • The seat has a capture radius, and aiming the body centre spends it on the lean. 50 mm of tip lever turns 8° into 7 mm (enters) and 14° into 12 mm (misses); every plate-25 chain that held the turn staged at 14–27° and missed the hole when the body centre was the aim point. Aiming the measured apex and taking the lean out about the seated tip lands all three within 1.5 mm and hands over at 0.4–6.3°; the lean at the end of the turn costs nothing at the seat once the trajectory is written for the tip.
  • The calibrated servo needs a command it can reach; after an RL turn it has one it cannot. The frozen residual leaves the thumb 70–79° past its achieved angle on the 0.35 N·m ceiling, and every command-referenced composition downstream (regrip, relay, gait table) keeps it there; an achieved-angle loop adds nothing to a stalled servo. Re-seeding from the achieved angles at the press takes the servos off the ceiling; the gait ring is then the next unreachable command (17–27 mm of IK residual on every D5/D6 run, including the 09-06 chain that read as solved on kp 30).
  • Unattended follow-ups. Two of three scheduled session wake-ups never fired; the page build has to live in the detached driver (or a watcher beside it), not in the session.

Next steps

  1. Finish the queue and rank on the jittered hold (remaining jobs listed in queue.json); the bench candidate is the hand whose continued policy holds ≥ 60 of 64 jittered and holds the chain at both plate heights.
  2. Turn quality on the matched plant. The continued policies end at cos 0.82–0.83 where their parents ended at 0.92–0.96: 20 M steps of continuation on a harder tool contact and a heavier tip is not yet converged, or the jitter costs turn. One 60 M continuation of the D6 separation job decides which.
  3. A gait ring the fingers can reach, at the palm pose the seat leaves. Solve the ring per hand (_ring_here on the pads’ own azimuths, ring depth and radius chosen for an IK residual under 2 mm at the current palm pose) before the relay walks the pads onto it; accept ring_ik_grip_mm < 2 and the index’s set-point error < 10° at handover_index. The alternative that needs no handover: gait on the contact set the press leaves (pads where they are, stroke about the tool axis, commands re-seeded from the achieved angles each cycle with the angle loop on), which turned 2–6° per cycle whenever the servos were off the ceiling. Accept ≥ 0.5 rev in 8 cycles on D6.
  4. Make --seat-aim tip --press-regrip 10 the driver’s default for the next tranche (the remaining rows of this one keep the shipped settings so the table stays comparable), and run it across the spawn-jitter seeds (--jitter, --seed on the probe) to get a rate rather than three single rollouts.
  5. Driver hygiene. --video on the driver’s chain call so every job gets its chain film; apply --seed in rl_train_cube.py (a dead flag today) after the queue; a second draw of the D4 job is queued (r_d4_clip_s1) to tell a stochastic NaN from the D4 pads on the mesh tool.
  6. The bench controller. A policy-driven station loop (servo telemetry + the AprilTag pose at 50 Hz → the 66-dim observation → the residual on the finger set-points), after the tracker’s x/y heading calibration. Nothing here has run on hardware.
  7. The privileged-critic blind actor (proprioception + motor load + history, critic with the pose), from scratch on the matched plant, once a sighted policy has been shown to transfer.
  8. Clearance threshold from a caliper on the built index and middle housings, then the separation weight sweep (−3 … −10) on D4 and D7 only.
  9. The friction rows of the 2026-09-17 D6 page re-run under the fixed variant (GPU).
